content:
- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks, especially in early 30d window.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model underestimates lows; increase forecast lows, especially in late 30d window.
- Model often overshoots after sharp sentiment spikes (e.g., sentiment jumps to 1.00), leading to overprediction; apply dampening factor to post-spike forecasts.
- Mean reversion is evident: if forecast is far above or below 1.5–2.0 range, adjust toward historical mean (last 5–10 days) unless sentiment strongly supports deviation.
- For 30d horizon, model frequently fails to capture short-term sentiment-driven reversals; add lagged sentiment smoothing (e.g., 3-day moving average) to forecast adjustments.
- When sentiment history shows repeated low values (e.g., 0.00 or 0.33), model underperforms; increase forecast sensitivity to sentiment decay, especially in 10–20d window.
